newsitem.title: USA: Big oil stocks fade from mid-day highs.
newsitem.headline: Big oil stocks fade from mid-day highs.

text.p: The stocks of major oil companies trimmed early gains in active afternoon trading after posting solid early gains on news Schroder Wertheim continues to overweight the group.

Analyst Michael Mayer cited first quarter adjusted earnings gains of 21 percent for the group in the first quarter and said those results continue to show the industry's high level of sustainable profitability.
Other analysts, however, felt most of the activity was not oil related, explaining it came from traders looking for stable, liquid stocks "who might be disappointed by year end."
Mayer called Unocal a strong outperfrom and its stock was still up 1-1/8 at 38-1/8 after trading as high as 38-5/8 on turnover of more than a million shares.

Exxon was among the stocks he rated outperform and it traded at a new year high of 57 before easing to 56-1/4, up 5/8, in late trading on news of a second dividend increase in as many years. More than 3.1 million shares had changed hands.

Also heavily traded was Chevron with turnover approaching 1.4 million shares in late trading. The stock was not on Mayer's list and its price was off 1/4 to 67-5/8 in late trading after reaching 68-7/8 earlier.

Among Mayer's outperform group were Mobil, which was holding on to half its early three point gain; Arco, still up 1-1/4 after being up 2-7/8; Royal Dutch, which was holding on to 3/8s of a 1-3/8 point gain; and Texaco, up one in late trading after rising 2-1/4 to 106-3/4 earlier. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
